Avg_Cost: $9,325 single / $26,993 family premium (employee pays ~$1,368 single / $6,296 family)
Key_Issue: Deductible burden ($1,886 avg single); rising premiums (+5-6% YoY); GLP-1 pushing Rx costs. 23% of employer-insured are underinsured.
Policy_Risk: Employer cost increases passed to workers via higher premiums and deductibles; GLP-1 coverage decisions splitting workforce access
Notes: Largest coverage type. Deductible inflation is the slow squeeze — insured but functionally underinsured for many. GLP-1 creating new intra-workforce access gap.

Avg_Cost: Avg silver plan deductible $5,304; bronze $7,186; premiums doubled for avg subsidized enrollee after subsidy lapse
Key_Issue: ACUTE CRISIS: enhanced subsidies expired Dec 31, 2025. 9% of prior enrollees now uninsured. Premiums +114% for avg subsidized enrollee.
Policy_Risk: Enhanced ACA tax credits EXPIRED — Congress declined to reinstate. Urban Institute: 4.8M newly uninsured in 2026. Premium doubling causing coverage loss cascade.
Source: CMS 2026 enrollment; KFF Jan 2026; CNBC Mar 2026
Notes: Most critical 2026 coverage trigger. Self-employed, gig workers, early retirees (age 55-64) hardest hit. ACA deductibles much higher than employer plans — creates high OOP risk for those who stay enrolled.

Key_Issue: 25M disenrolled during unwinding (2023-2025); 31% termination rate; most transitioned to other coverage but ~5M estimated coverage gap
Policy_Risk: Budget reconciliation 2026 may include work requirements or per-capita caps. Medicaid expansion rollbacks in some states.

Policy_Risk: IRA drug provisions could be rolled back by new administration; Medicare Advantage overpayment scrutiny
Notes: IRA provisions are meaningful for Medicare population but scope limited (10 drugs, Medicare only). Does not affect commercial insurance. Positive counter-signal vs thesis for this cohort only.

Avg_Cost: Technically insured but high OOP relative to income: deductible >5% income OR OOP >10% income
Key_Issue: 23% of insured Americans underinsured (Commonwealth Fund 2024). 66% have employer coverage. 57% of underinsured forgo needed care. Functionally uninsured for most healthcare.
Policy_Risk: No direct policy risk — underinsurance is structural result of HDHP expansion. Deductible inflation will worsen.
Notes: This is the CARL-relevant cohort: has insurance card but can't afford to use it. Creates hidden care deferral in "insured" population. POLLY overlap — tracks via deductible and OOP max data.
